advisor_identified: Jeremy L. Caradonna, associate professor of History and Classics at the University of Alberta, later teaching Environmental Studies at the University of Victoria.

doctorate.title: The Enlightenment in Question: Prize Contests and the Francophone Republic of Letters, 1670-1794

evidence.says: The 2015–16 University of Alberta staff directory, PDF page 5, lists Jeremy Caradonna as Associate Professor of History and Classics with an MA and PhD from Johns Hopkins.

David A. Bell’s CV, page 37, lists doctoral student Jeremy Caradonna (Johns Hopkins University, 2007), formerly a tenured associate professor at Alberta; his revised thesis became The Enlightenment in Practice (Cornell University Press, 2012).

Caradonna’s article in Annales, volume 64 (2009), footnote 7, cites Jeremy L. Caradonna’s The Enlightenment in Question: Prize Contests (Concours Académiques) and the Francophone Republic of Letters, 1670-1794 as a PhD dissertation, Johns Hopkins University, 2007.

The contributor biography in the licensed preview of History of the Future of Economic Growth, PDF page 9, states that Jeremy L. Caradonna received his history PhD from Johns Hopkins University in 2007 and taught history at Alberta before Environmental Studies at Victoria.

notes: The linked record matches the advisor’s name, history department, institution, year and dissertation title. His own article adds the explanatory parenthetical “Concours Académiques” to the title. The 2015–16 Alberta directory establishes the affiliation corresponding to the supplied student record.
